text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (also known as Suboptimal Intake Jaundice)

The history of increasing yellowing at 2 weeks of age, combined with exclusive breastfeeding and a weight gain consistent with normal recovery (from 3066g to 3200g), strongly suggests this diagnosis. The lack of mention of poor stooling or feeding issues in the script supports this, as these conditions typically present earlier or with more severe feeding difficulties. I have already requested the Total Serum Bilirubin level to quantify the bilirubin load and rule out hemolytic causes; pending those results, I will focus on assessing hydration and feeding frequency.
